title: David: Name Meaning, Origin & Personality
summary: David is a timeless and enduring classic cherished across the globe for its strength and simplicity. It offers a wonderful blend of deep historical roots and modern warmth for a baby boy.
origin: David is an ancient Hebrew name with clear Semitic roots, traditionally translated to mean 'beloved.' Its history spans thousands of years, emerging from the ancient Near East and spreading widely through historical texts and global trade routes. Today, it remains exceptionally popular across Europe, the Americas, and parts of the Middle East, beloved by parents who appreciate traditional names that transcend cultural and linguistic boundaries while maintaining their original charm and dignity.
personality: In popular culture and folklore, the name David is often associated with steadfast loyalty, quiet confidence, and natural leadership. People with this name are frequently viewed as dependable friends, thoughtful problem solvers, and creative thinkers. There is a grounded, reassuring energy linked to David, suggesting someone who approaches life with integrity, resilience, and a caring heart. This positive perception makes the name a wonderful choice for parents hoping to inspire kindness and inner strength in their child.
popularity: David is a perpetual favorite that has rarely left mainstream naming charts in Western societies. It enjoys widespread popularity in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia, as well as throughout Scandinavia and Eastern Europe. Because it is neither overly trendy nor excessively rare, it strikes a universally appealing chord with parents seeking a name that is both familiar and distinguished.

faq.q: Is David considered a traditional name?
faq.ans: Yes, David is one of the most enduring traditional names in recorded history. It has maintained steady popularity across centuries without ever feeling dated.

faq.q: What are the most common nicknames for David?
faq.ans: The most frequent and friendly short forms are Dave and Davey. Both offer a casual, approachable alternative to the full name.

faq.q: Does David work well with middle names?
faq.ans: Because of its classic two-syllable rhythm and familiar ending, David pairs wonderfully with almost any middle name. It flows easily with both short, punchy syllables and longer, flowing choices.

faq.q: How is David pronounced in different languages?
faq.ans: While English speakers typically say DAY-vid, European variants like Davide or Dawid offer slight variations in vowel sounds and stress. Every version maintains the same warm, recognizable cadence.
